entry.title: Simplifying 2-Bundle Descriptions of Invariants and Local Dynamics
entry.summary: A string couples to a two-form gauge potential whose local descriptions need not fit together as a single global form. Principal 2-bundles provide a geometric description of this gluing. However, we recover surface amplitudes and quantum partition functions, as well as local classical field dynamics, without the 2-bundle formalism. For global phases, topological and index invariants, and twisted-sheaf moduli, established equivalences give alternative descriptions through cocycles, bundles, operators, or modules, with the required global compatibility data. For three-dimensional finite gauge theories with cohomological actions, Fourier transformation expresses the partition function as a sum of partition functions of ordinary finite-group gauge theories. An invertible local substitution reduces invariant classical actions for a class of 2-bundle connections represented by finite-dimensional crossed modules to ordinary gauge and tensor dynamics. These finite and local reductions explicitly eliminate field variables. A four-dimensional quadratic example instead admits a direct cochain evaluation even when an ordinary gauge-theory reduction fails. These results therefore do not require the additional 2-bundle presentation.

entry.title: Primordial Black Hole Seeds for Little Red Dots in $f(R)$ Gravity
entry.summary: The little red dots (LRDs) discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope host black holes of up to $10^{9}\,M_{\odot}$ within the first billion years, posing a challenge to conventional seeding scenarios. We investigate whether such seeds can form in dense clusters of primordial black holes (PBHs), in which the central object grows by gravitational capture of the surrounding PBHs while accreting gas, within Hu-Sawicki $f(R)$ gravity, where the scalar field acts on the matter surrounding the PBHs. For the adopted cluster configuration, our results show that accretion and mergers reinforce one another: for time-averaged Eddington ratios $λ_{\rm Edd}\gtrsim0.3$, the seed consumes its cluster by $z\simeq5.5$-$7.3$ and subsequently grows into the LRD mass range. Calibrated on the observed black-hole mass function, the model reproduces the abundance of LRDs near the peak of their population without further adjustment, while it underpredicts the abundance at $z\simeq7.5$ and overpredicts it at $z\simeq2$. Our findings indicate that the earliest seeds may accrete about twice as efficiently as later ones, and that the finite cluster reservoir can imprint a lower edge on the mass function near the cluster mass. Within the adopted screening and halo-growth prescriptions, the scalar field enhances the abundance of active seeds by up to $\sim 13\%$ at lower redshifts and by $\sim 7\%$ at $z \simeq 7.5$ for the strongest model considered, modestly moving the high-redshift prediction towards the data at fixed normalization. Also, the remnant spins can further discriminate between feeding modes.

entry.title: Derivation of OH sum rules without Rayleigh--Jeans approximation: a powerful tool for measuring the variation of fundamental physical constants
entry.summary: In this paper, we show that the optical depths of any OH $Λ$-doublet quartet obey one exact linear relation in every velocity channel. No approximation is needed. The only exception is the $^{2}Π_{1/2}$ $J{=}1/2$ level, which has three transitions only, because its $F{=}0{\leftrightarrow}0$ line is strictly forbidden. The relation is $τ_{S_1}(v)/μ_{S_1}^{2}+τ_{S_2}(v)/μ_{S_2}^{2}=τ_{M_1}(v)/(aμ_{M_1}^{2})+τ_{M_2}(v)/(bμ_{M_2}^{2})$, where $a=2J^{2}+J-1$, $b=2J^{2}+3J$, and the $μ_i^{2}$ are reduced transition dipole moments derived from the catalogued Einstein $A$ coefficients. It holds equally for gas in local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), for non-LTE gas, for masers and for conjugate gas. We suggest that it is a powerful tool for measuring the variation of fundamental physical constants.

entry.title: Twirled Perfect Tensor Networks: Computationally covariant holographic tensor networks
entry.summary: We define a novel class of tensor networks motivated by the Python's Lunch Conjecture (PLC) in local tensor network models of the black hole interior. We start from the observation that, for extended black brane states with short-range correlations, the PLC predicts a complexity that is smaller than the upper bound for generic short-range correlated states. We argue that the PLC makes implicit assumptions about the fine structure of the relevant tensor networks modeling gravity that render them non-generic. We demonstrate this explicitly in random tensor network models of the python's lunch, where the exponential complexity is not generally controlled by the PLC exponent. We trace the difference with the PLC to a lack of "computational covariance" in random tensor networks: while the PLC is motivated by an ability to arbitrarily decompose space into low-complexity units provided certain basic rules are followed, we show that random tensor networks do not generically have this property. We propose another class of tensor networks built from what we call "twirled perfect tensors" that do satisfy the computational covariance property and have a complexity bounded by the PLC value. We still find a discrete limitation from local postselection that appears to be absent in gravity. Moreover, we show that this class of tensor networks combines desirable holographic features of perfect tensor networks and random tensor networks, for example, it obeys a lattice Ryu-Takayanagi formula for arbitrary boundary subregions. Though motivated by holography, these tensor networks provide a flexible framework with potential applications beyond quantum gravity.

entry.title: Axion Inflation: Perturbative control in the strong backreaction regime
entry.summary: We study the strong backreaction regime in axion inflation, in which the friction from Abelian gauge fields generated via the pseudo-scalar interaction $\fracβ{4 M_p} φF {\tilde F}$ is comparable to Hubble friction. The non-linear dynamics associated with the gauge fields render this regime phenomenologically particularly interesting, but also notoriously difficult to study with perturbative methods. Quantifying the perturbative control through the direct impact on the spectral backreaction using (i) a first-order gradient-expansion formalism including axion gradients, and (ii) a one-loop in-in calculation, we discover an extended mild backreaction regime at large couplings $β$, with a relatively large, nearly constant particle production parameter $ξ$. In passing, we point out that CMB non-Gaussianity bounds impose a general upper limit on the product of axion gauge field coupling and Hubble parameter during inflation, $βH/M_p < 1.4\cdot 10^{-3}$, independently of the choice of the axion potential.

entry.title: The long-term evolution of a black hole accretion torus: a comparison between GRMHD simulations and relativistic thin disk theory
entry.summary: In this paper we analyse the long-term evolution of a black hole accretion torus using novel GRMHD simulations which, for the first time, have been run out to extremely large evolutionary times $t_{\rm max} = 10^7 GM_\bullet/c^3$. This allows for detailed comparisons between the gross evolution of this GRMHD simulation and existing "spreading disk" analytical theories. We show that the long-term features of this evolution are well described by General Relativistic Thin Disk Theory (GRTDT), which reproduces various aspects of the GRMHD evolution to within a factor $\sim 2$, despite the disk in our simulation not being remotely thin, showing dynamically dominant (MAD) magnetic fields, and launching a powerful wind. Thin disk theory functions as an accurate and cheap effective theory for the evolution in radius and time of the bulk of the disk material, and for the time dependence of the horizon accretion rate. We argue that this effectiveness originates from the global conservation laws of mass and angular momentum, together with a turbulent stress which we find to be local and independent of density, lending support to the ad-hoc local-stress-tensor phenomenology employed in analytical models. We also find that the turbulent accretion rate variability in the inner disk is log-normally distributed, consistent with a key assumption in the modeling of observed variability.

entry.title: Sensing the Inflationary Production of Scalars
entry.summary: We review the mechanism by which loops of matter fields contribute to the graviton self-energy during de Sitter inflation. This self-energy is used to quantum-correct the linearized Einstein equations. A Green's function method is employed to obtain exact 1-loop corrections to the plane wave mode functions of gravitational radiation, subject to the usual ambiguity in the initial state. Conformally coupled matter, which does not experience inflationary particle production, makes only a logarithmic enhancement of the rate at which the imaginary part of the mode function goes to zero after horizon crossing. These corrections can be understood, and even summed up, using a variant of the renormalization group. However, massless, minimally coupled scalars, which experience massive inflationary particle production, induce a much stronger enhancement of the rate at which the real part of the mode function approaches a constant. One interpretation of this effect is as a shift of the inflationary Hubble parameter.

entry.title: Indication of Electron Antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background
entry.summary: We report an indication of $\barν_e$ from the diffuse supernova neutrino background (DSNB) based on a spectral fit analysis of a 5003.0-day dataset in Super-Kamiokande. Key improvements over previous searches include enhanced rejection of atmospheric $ν$ backgrounds, updated evaluations of systematic uncertainties, and a refined spectral fitting method. Using a representative DSNB model, the best-fit flux was determined to be $3.6^{+1.6}_{-1.5}~\mathrm{cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ for $E_ν>13.3$~MeV, corresponding to a $2.6σ$ tension with a null hypothesis ($99.5\%$ C.L., one-sided). Similar significances were obtained with signal models of varying spectral shapes.

entry.title: Nonlinear Tides of Binary Neutron Stars
entry.summary: Nonlinear tides couple stellar oscillations and reshape the gravitational wave (GW) signal from inspiralling binaries. We present hydrodynamic simulations of nonlinear tides in inspiralling neutron-star binaries and, within a mode-coupling model, derive a semi-analytic quadrupolar fundamental mode-frequency shift through second order in the tidal strength. The two approaches agree in the perturbative regime, but diverge at stronger tidal fields, where perturbation theory breaks down. In the late inspiral, nonlinear tides reduce the fundamental-mode frequency by ${\sim}10\%$ for equal-mass binaries and add a GW phase shift of $\mathcal{O}(1)$ radian beyond the linear tidal response. These effects make nonlinear tides a promising target for next-generation GW detectors.

entry.title: Designing Strongly Correlated Quantum Phases of Matter with Foundation Neural-Network Quantum States
entry.summary: Materials design is an inverse problem: finding the couplings of a microscopic Hamiltonian whose ground state exhibits a desired property. For strongly correlated quantum systems, this remains largely out of reach, as each candidate Hamiltonian requires its own costly simulation. Here we show that Foundation Neural-Network Quantum States, single wave functions that encode the ground states of an entire family of Hamiltonians, make this search efficient. Because the Hamiltonian couplings enter as neural-network inputs, any ground-state property can be optimized by gradient descent directly in coupling space. We use this approach to search for nonmagnetic phases in two-dimensional spin models in coupling spaces of increasing dimensionality. Specifically, we focus on quantum spin liquids, exotic phases of matter in which quantum fluctuations prevent magnetic order at zero temperature. In the largest search space considered, spanned by eight superexchange couplings and containing many paradigmatic frustrated spin systems, the optimization converges to the $J_1$-$J_2$-$δ$ Heisenberg model when starting from a magnetic phase. We show that the ground state at the optimum set of couplings has neither magnetic nor valence-bond order in the thermodynamic limit, leading to a new quantum spin-liquid candidate. The approach is completely general and can be extended to other models and physical properties to optimize, demonstrating that Neural-Network Quantum States are tools not only for simulating quantum matter but also for designing it.

entry.title: Variable-mass sine-Gordon with point defects: integrability, soliton transmission, and quasi-conservation
entry.summary: We study integrable variable-mass sine-Gordon model (vmSG) with point defects. Using the Lax and Bäcklund-gauge formulations, we construct type-I and type-II defect matrices, derive the corresponding sewing conditions, and generate the bulk and defect contributions to an infinite hierarchy of conserved charges. The lowest members reduce to the standard sine-Gordon energy and momentum in the homogeneous limit, while for inhomogeneous backgrounds they define integrability-generated energy- and momentum-type quantities. Defect compatibility imposes matching conditions on the variable-mass functions across the defect. An analytical transmission factor $z$ characterizes soliton transmission, topological conversion, and absorption/emission processes. We then deform the type-I sewing conditions by parameters $α$ and $β$ and derive the associated defect anomalies. Consistent one-soliton transmission is recovered for $αβ=1$, whereas for $αβ\neq 1$ parity-centered kink-kink and kink-antikink transmissions display vanishing lowest order integrated anomalies but no generic vanishing at higher order. Numerical simulations reproduce the integrable transmission/conversion regimes and show that non-integrable defects generate small residual disturbances and lowest order quasi-conserved charges, while quasi-conservation of the higher order charges remains unestablished. These results elucidate how exact defect integrability deforms into charge-dependent quasi-conservation and establish a framework for defect-controlled soliton transport in inhomogeneous media, with potential applications to nonuniform Josephson junctions, magnetic and nonlinear-optical systems, and effective molecular and DNA models.

entry.title: Gravitationally Induced Polarization-Angle Rotation in Pulsar-Black Hole Binaries
entry.summary: Radio pulsars emit highly polarized radiation whose polarization properties are commonly described by the Rotating Vector Model (RVM). In this work, we investigate the effects of gravitational light bending and parallel transport on the polarization profile of a pulsar in a hypothetical binary system with a black hole (BH) companion. We combine the RVM with numerical integration of null geodesics to calculate the polarization direction along the photon trajectory and model the orbital-phase-dependent variation of the observed polarization position angle (PPA). We consider both non-spinning and spinning black hole companions and include the evolution of the orbital geometry due to relativistic spin-orbit coupling. For a non-spinning black hole, the change in the observed polarization direction arises from the geometric shift associated with gravitational light bending. For a spinning black hole, frame dragging introduces an additional geometric shift, while parallel transport produces an additional polarization rotation measured relative to our chosen reference construction. We investigate the dependence of these polarization changes on the binary parameters and the orientation of the pulsar spin. We find that gravitational light bending can significantly distort the characteristic S-shaped PPA profile, particularly near superior conjunction, and can reverse its overall sense of variation for the supermassive black hole system considered here. Relativistic spin-orbit evolution also affects the orbital-phase dependence of the polarization profile, particularly in the supermassive black hole system. These results show that relativistic photon propagation can modify both the shape and the phase dependence of pulsar polarization profiles and may provide a useful probe of the geometry of pulsar-BH binaries when such systems are discovered.

entry.title: p-Wave Dominant Majorana Dark Matter and Its Self-Interactions in a Gauged $U(1)_{L_μ- L_τ}$ Model
entry.summary: We propose a model of $p$-wave dominant Majorana dark matter (DM) featuring a macroscopic mass gap in a gauged $U(1)_{L_μ- L_τ}$ extension of the Standard Model. Spontaneous symmetry breaking generates a dominant Majorana mass via a strong Yukawa coupling, splitting the dark fermion into two distinct states. The lighter state ($χ_-$) is the DM candidate, with an allowed mass of $\sim 10$ GeV to several hundred GeV. Crucially, within the $10 \sim 75$ GeV mass range and a scalar mediator at the tens of MeV scale, this strong coupling dictates the thermal relic abundance and induces significant elastic self-interactions. These self-interactions naturally resolve small-scale structure anomalies, such as the core-cusp problem, while satisfying massive cluster constraints. Furthermore, we place stringent joint constraints on the scalar mass and the Higgs mixing angle $α$ using the latest LZ 2025 direct detection data. The model's gauge boson $Z^\prime$ maintains early-Universe thermal equilibrium and accommodates the muon anomalous magnetic moment $(g-2)_μ$, remaining consistent with updated cosmological and experimental bounds.

entry.title: Web of Non-invertible Dualities for (2+1) Dimensional Models with Subsystem Symmetries
entry.summary: We extend non-invertible duality concepts from one-dimensional systems to two spatial dimensions by constructing a web of non-invertible dualities for lattice models with subsystem symmetries. For the $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2$ subsystem symmetry on the square lattice, we build two complementary dualities: a map that sends spontaneous subsystem symmetry-broken (SSSB) phases to the trivial phase (the analogue of the Kramers-Wannier (KW) duality in 1+1D), and a generalized subsystem Kennedy-Tasaki (KT) transformation that maps SSSB phases to subsystem symmetry-protected topological (SSPT) phases while leaving the trivial phase invariant. These dualities are boundary-sensitive. On open lattices, both subsystem KW and KT transformations act as unitary, invertible operators. In particular, the KT map not only matches the bulk Hamiltonians of the dual phases but also carries the spontaneous ground-state degeneracy of the SSSB phase onto the protected boundary degeneracy of the SSPT phase. On closed manifolds, however, both maps become intrinsically non-unitary and non-invertible when restricted to the original Hilbert space. We demonstrate this non-invertibility via ground-state degeneracy matching (in two copies of the Xu-Moore/Ising-plaquette model), analysis of symmetry-twist sectors mapping, and the fusion algebra of the duality operator. Enlarging the Hilbert space to include twisted sectors allows the subsystem KW map to be formulated as a projective unitary preserving quantum transition probabilities, consistent with generalized Wigner-theorem-based constructions. We also show that the KT map faithfully transmits the algebraic content of bulk and edge invariants diagnosing strong SSPT order: although strictly local SSPT repair operators map to highly nonlocal objects in the dual SSSB phase, the essential commutation algebra and the bulk-edge correspondence remain intact.

entry.title: Forward Bayesian Inference for the Binary Black Hole Populations
entry.summary: We present PopCWB, a Bayesian framework for the inference of the binary black hole (BBH) population based on the unmodeled search pipeline coherent WaveBurst (cWB). The standard population analysis takes an inverse approach by inferring the underlying population model parameters for a given set of detected events using the individual posterior samples. In PopCWB, we take a forward approach to population inference by varying population models to identify the most optimal one which describes the observed events. Rather than using event-level posterior samples, PopCWB uses a large set of simulated events reconstructed by cWB and their total mass, estimated with a machine-learning regression, to construct marginal probability distributions. These marginal probabilities are then used in the construction of the likelihood. We apply PopCWB to BBH events detected by cWB during the third observing run (O3) of the LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA detectors. We constrain an astrophysically motivated BBH population model that incorporates the effects of pulsational pair-instability supernovae and dynamical mergers. The analysis predicts a maximum black hole mass of $\mathbf{45.5^{+5.1}_{-6.1} M_{\odot}}$ from stellar evolution and an inferred local BBH merger rate of $\mathbf{23.0^{+16.6}_{-8.3} \, Gpc^{-3} yr^{-1}}$. We compare these results with the existing population models from the literature.

entry.title: Classification of Fermi Blazars of Uncertain Type Using Positive-Unlabelled Machine Learning
entry.summary: We apply positive-unlabelled (PU) machine learning to the 1623 blazars of uncertain type (BCUs) in the Fermi Large Area Telescope Fourth Source Catalogue, Data Release 4 (4FGL-DR4). Five PU classifiers are trained on seven gamma-ray features, once with the 820 flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs) and once with the 1490 BL Lac objects as the labelled class (FSRQ mode and BL Lac mode). Each source is scored out of fold over 100 repeated five-fold splits, and its confidence is the fraction of splits in which at least three of the five classifiers flag it. At a confidence of at least 0.1, 437 BCUs are FSRQ-like, 597 are BL Lac-like, 12 are flagged in both modes and 577 in neither. On known sources the ensemble reaches a recall of 0.80 in FSRQ mode and 0.82 in BL Lac mode at a false-positive rate of 0.08, but a logistic regression trained on the labelled sources alone does at least as well, so PU learning gives no accuracy gain here. Removing the sky coordinates from the features does not lower the performance on known sources but adds 107 BCUs to the candidate lists and drops 30, which is consistent with the coordinates acting as a selection shortcut, so we exclude them. We check the candidates against published optical spectra, SDSS-V spectra, and BCUs that later received a class in the catalogue. Among sources assigned a single class, BL Lac-like calls are correct for 84 to 100% of the sources and FSRQ-like calls for 58 to 83%, depending on the sample. These samples come from spectroscopic follow-up and do not represent all BCUs. The candidates are fainter and lie closer to the Galactic plane than the labelled sources, and the excess of unclassified BCUs in the plane is not explained. We release the confidences of all 1623 BCUs.

entry.title: Extracting intrinsic alignments in the Dark Energy Survey's year 1 data, using the self-calibration method and LSST-DESC tools
entry.summary: We present the implementation of a Self-Calibration of Intrinsic Alignments of galaxies as an extension to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) Dark Energy Science Collaboration (DESC)'s weak lensing 3x2pt pipeline (TXPipe). As a demonstration, we have run this pipeline on the Dark Energy Survey (DES) year one data set. We find indications of a non-zero intrinsic alignment signal in the higher redshift bins, while in the lower bins our results look more uncertain. We believe this is caused by known issues with the individual galaxies photo-z estimation. This effect is particularly harmful for the self-calibration method, since it has high requirements for reliable estimation of the photo-$z$s, and the need for individual galaxy point estimates and tomographic binning to match. We show how different methods of recreating the redshift probability distribution can affect the detection of intrinsic alignment.

entry.title: Quantum state revivals, time quasicrystals, and entanglement steering in a Fibonacci-driven central-spin model
entry.summary: Motivated by the search for non-equilibrium phases of matter beyond the Floquet paradigm, we propose a route to realize perfect revivals and time quasicrystals (TQCs) in a Fibonacci-driven central-spin model with Ising interactions between the central and satellite spins in the absence of disorder. We analytically demonstrate that when the interaction strength, $λ$ is tuned to $2 m π$, no entanglement is generated between the central and satellite spins at stroboscopic times, independent of the strength of the transverse driving field and the drive sequence. This leads to indefinitely long-lived quasiperiodic oscillations in satellite spin magnetization. Furthermore, for initial states with a definite bath magnetization, no entanglement is generated when the transverse driving field, $θ$ is tuned to $π$ for any value of $ λ$, and the satellite spin magnetization oscillations exhibit period-3 revivals at Fibonacci times. Examining the robustness of these oscillations away from this fine-tuned limit, we identify a parameter regime where the quasiperiodic response does not decay over the timescales probed, giving rise to a long-lived $π$-pulse-proximate TQC regime. We further show that at special Clifford points, the system exhibits perfect quasiperiodic oscillations of the satellite spin magnetization, with a parity-dependent Fourier response. This response persists over the timescales probed, even away from the Clifford points for an even number of satellite spins, leading to the formation of a Clifford-proximate TQC. Finally, we demonstrate that at this Clifford points, the system is steered along an entangled trajectory, leading to the dynamical generation of Bell-cat and spin-cat states. These states exhibit magnetization of collective spin fluctuates quadratically with the number of satellite spins, thereby enabling Heisenberg-limited metrology.

entry.title: Constraints on Horndeski gravity with phantom crossing
entry.summary: Gravity models in which the dark energy equation of state crosses $w=-1$, also known as the phantom divide, have received extensive interest due to recent analyses favouring this behaviour. We introduce a new subclass of Horndeski scalar-tensor models capable of generating phantom crossing, whilst remaining minimally coupled to matter: the Asymptotic Cubic Galileon (ACG) models. We show that ACG models can jointly fit the expansion history inferred from observations of the Planck cosmic microwave background, baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument, and distance-ladder supernovae measurements from the Dark Energy Survey. We then demonstrate that requiring a positive galaxy-ISW cross-correlation, together with physically viable screening behaviour, substantially restricts the viable ACG parameter space. Model comparison metrics, including $χ^{2}$ and Bayesian evidence, favour both ACG and $w_{0}w_{a}$CDM models over $Λ$CDM, with ACG providing a fit of comparable quality to $w_{0}w_{a}$CDM. Crucially, ACG models ground the observationally preferred $w_{0}w_{a}$CDM behaviour in a robust Lagrangian formulation. This enables interpretation beyond mere phenomenological fits, and motivates further tests of these models on nonlinear scales.

entry.title: An Intermediate Mass Stripped Star in a 4.2-hour Orbit around a Compact Object
entry.summary: From their discovery as radio pulsars to landmark multi-messenger observations of their mergers, double neutron stars have transformed our understanding of the extreme Universe and the formation of heavy elements (Drout et al. 2017; Abbott et al. 2017). Yet, uncertainties in their formation result in predicted merger rates spanning orders of magnitude (Tauris et al. 2017; Mandel & Broekgaarden 2022). The most critical stage occurs when a star is stripped of its hydrogen-rich envelope, causing the binary orbit to shrink drastically. Despite its fundamental role, the resulting tight binaries comprising a stripped star and neutron star have remained elusive. Here we report a $\sim$$3.4\,M_{\odot}$ stripped star (Ludwig et al. 2026; Drout et al. 2023; Götberg et al. 2023) orbiting an unseen companion every 4.2 hours. Our orbital and spectroscopic analysis excludes a normal star, which would not fit within the orbit, as well as a second stripped star which would have been detectable in our spectra. Adding constraints from high cadence photometry gives a 99.4% probability that the companion is too massive to be a white dwarf, making a neutron star the most likely companion. We model the system's future and predict that the stripped star will transfer mass again before exploding as a hydrogen-free supernova, leaving a bound pair of neutron stars that will merge after 220 Myr. This system reveals a previously unconstrained phase of binary evolution, uncovering a new class of systems that probes the uncertain physics of massive stars, linking to observable gravitational-wave sources.

entry.title: Inverse KLT kernel of AdS string integrals from the intersection matrix
entry.summary: We develop a topological and combinatorial interpretation of the Kawai--Lewellen--Tye (KLT) relations for $n$-point AdS string-amplitude building blocks, which are disk integrals with multivariable multiple polylogarithm insertions and sphere integrals with their single-valued counterparts. Building on the framework of twisted de Rham theory over a noncommutative ring, we reformulate the problem in terms of associahedral chambers of the moduli space loaded with solutions of the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equation. We construct regularized twisted cycles and express their intersection pairings through local monodromies and Drinfeld associators, which control transport between fusion-tree normalizations. Organizing the intersection contributions by common boundary faces yields the intersection matrix, which is identified with the inverse KLT kernel by the twisted period relation. The field-theory limit of the inverse KLT kernel is also given.

entry.title: Cavity control of quantum phase transitions in a two-dimensional Kondo lattice
entry.summary: Cavity quantum electrodynamics offers a route to control quantum phases by using vacuum fluctuations of confined electromagnetic fields. In particular, planar cavities based on polar van der Waals materials can generate strongly confined modes and are promising for controlling two-dimensional correlated materials. Recently, moiré materials have become central platforms for studying two-dimensional heavy-fermion systems and their quantum phase transitions. Kondo lattices provide a prototypical model for studying quantum phase boundaries, driven by competition between Kondo screening and the ordering of local magnetic moments. We show that a cavity-induced interaction can shift the quantum phase transitions between a heavy-fermion phase and an antiferromagnetic phase in a two-dimensional Kondo lattice through a momentum-dependent self-energy of the conduction bands. For the longitudinal projected field motivated by h-BN hyperbolic phonon polaritons, the self-energy favors Kondo hybridization and expands the heavy-fermion region. Transverse and circular in-plane model structures give distinct effects, with the transverse case relatively favoring the magnetically ordered phase and the circular case lying between the longitudinal and transverse cases. These results indicate that electromagnetic vacuum fluctuations can effectively modify the control parameters of strongly correlated two-dimensional Kondo materials.

entry.title: Model-independent calibration of gamma-ray bursts with Bayesian neural networks
entry.summary: Context. Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) extend cosmological distance measurements beyond the range densely sampled by Type Ia supernovae, but their standardization requires reliable calibration and uncertainty estimates. Aims. We calibrate the Amati correlation without assuming a background cosmological model, assess its stability, and examine the cosmological reach of current and future GRB Hubble diagrams. Methods. We train a Bayesian neural network on Pantheon+ supernovae, assess and recalibrate its predictive uncertainties, and calibrate the correlation for GRBs at $z \leq 1.5$ using the D'Agostini and Reichart likelihoods. We combine the GRB Hubble diagram with supernovae, Hubble-parameter measurements, and DESI baryon acoustic oscillations. Local-regression, covariance, leave-three-out, redshift-evolution, and Efron-Petrosian diagnostics test the standardization assumptions. We also analyse idealized future catalogues of 1500 standardized GRBs. Results. The diagram reaches $z \simeq 9.4$. Covariance and leave-three-out diagnostics produce small changes in the cosmological constraints. A parametric evolution coefficient is consistent with zero, whereas the truncation-corrected diagnostic indicates marginal isotropic-energy evolution that can occur along the Amati relation. Dark-energy extensions improve the phenomenological fit relative to flat $Λ$CDM: AIC favours the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder parametrization, while BIC favours constant-$w$ dark energy. Forecasts show strong conditional model-discrimination power under the adopted uncertainty model. Conclusions. GRBs provide a complementary high-redshift extension of the supernova distance ladder. Present results do not establish an evolving dark-energy equation of state. Larger homogeneous samples are promising, but realistic selection functions and calibration systematics remain essential.

entry.title: A different kind of continuum limit for the three-dimensional U(1) gauge theory
entry.summary: In three-dimensional compact U(1) lattice gauge theory color confinement can be understood analytically through the dynamics of magnetic monopoles. However, its continuum limit is pathological, since the ratio of the glueball masses to the square root of the string tension vanishes as the continuum limit is approached. We investigate a simple extension of the Wilson action in which the total number of lattice monopoles is coupled to an additional parameter $μ$. By tuning $β$ and $μ$ simultaneously, we identify a line of constant physics along which the ratio of the lightest glueball mass to the square root of the string tension remains constant. We further show that the same scaling is satisfied, within numerical uncertainties, by the other low-lying glueball masses considered in this work. Along this trajectory, the string tension in lattice units decreases with increasing $β$, thus suggesting that the modified lattice action may provide a regularization of three-dimensional compact U(1) gauge theory with a physically well-behaved continuum limit.

entry.title: Quasibound modes of rotating acoustic black holes
entry.summary: In this paper, we introduce a metric describing rotating acoustic black holes in spherical coordinates. This formulation allows us to obtain exact analytical solutions of the massless Klein--Gordon equation governing scalar perturbations in the corresponding background spacetime. By imposing the appropriate boundary conditions, we derive an exact analytical expression for the quasibound state frequencies of the system. Quasibound states play a central role in the dynamics of black hole analog systems, as they characterize long-lived resonant modes trapped in the vicinity of the effective horizon. Their investigation provides valuable insights into wave propagation, mode stability, and energy confinement in analog spacetimes. Moreover, because acoustic black holes offer experimentally accessible realizations of horizon physics, the study of quasibound states may establish a direct connection between theoretical predictions and laboratory observations, thereby contributing to a deeper understanding of phenomena that also arise in gravitational black hole environments.

entry.title: The Dancing Bonfire: An Unusual Persistent X-ray Source in M81 Exhibiting Recurrent Luminous Flares
entry.summary: Short-timescale X-ray variability provides a direct probe of unstable accretion onto compact objects, yet extragalactic X-ray binaries (XRBs) with recurrent flaring remain largely unexplored. Here we present a detailed X-ray study of M81F4 (2CXO~J095524.2+690957), a persistently luminous X-ray source towards M81 that exhibits recurrent short X-ray flares. Based on multi-mission X-ray observations spanning two decades, it is found that M81F4 remains persistently bright at $L_{0.5-8.0\rm~keV}\sim10^{38}-10^{39}\rm~erg~s^{-1}$, while producing flares lasting a few hundred seconds and reaching peak luminosities of a few $10^{39}\rm~erg~s^{-1}$, with an observed mean (minimum) recurrence time of $\sim0.5$ day ($\sim$6 ks). The stacked flare profile shows a rapid rise followed by a slower decay, but no significant hardness evolution. Spectral analysis reveals that both the flare and non-flare states are dominated by a hard power-law continuum, with marginal evidence of highly ionized Fe lines in the non-flare state spectrum. These properties disfavor classical Type I and Type II bursts and have no close analog among known XRBs. We favor a magnetized neutron star accreting from an intermediate mass donor at a persistently high rate with the flares arising from instabilities at the disk-magnetosphere boundary. If confirmed, M81F4 might represent a hidden population of XRBs in which sustained, magnetically-regulated accretion can lead to brief episodes of super-Eddington emission.
entry.arxiv:comment: 22 pages, 6 figures. Accepted for publication in ApJ

entry.title: On the assessment of the disk truncation and detection of type-II-like bursts from the accreting millisecond X-ray Pulsar IGR J17062-6143
entry.summary: We present a spectral analysis of the NuSTAR and NICER observations of the accreting millisecond X-ray pulsar IGR J17062-6143, performed in 2022. The source remained in the hard spectral state during these observations, with a luminosity of about $\sim$0.13-0.14 percent of the Eddington luminosity. The continuum emission of the NuSTAR spectrum is entirely dominated by a power-law component or by Comptonized emission of disc photons by a plasma with a high electron temperature ($\gtrsim100$ keV). The NuSTAR spectrum also reveals clear evidence of disc reflection, a broad Fe K line around 6-8 keV, and a Compton hump peaking at 20 keV, irrespective of the choice of the continuum models. Our spectral studies suggest a disk extending close to the neutron star surface ($\sim$6-20 $R_{\rm g}$) at low inclination angle ($\sim41$ degrees), as revealed by the self-consistent relativistic reflection model, relxill. In addition, we detected type-II-like bursts for the first time in the NICER observation of this source. Light curve profiles of type-II-like bursts exhibit different patterns, mostly associated with the so-called mode-0 and transition from mode-0 to mode-1 type-II bursts. The energy spectra of the persistent (pre-burst) and burst emission are well described by an absorbed Comptonization component, scattering disk- and blackbody-distributed photons, respectively, by a corona with a temperature of 1-3 keV. Although the origin of the type-II-like burst is not very clear, it has been possibly linked to disk-magnetosphere interaction of the accretion flow.
entry.arxiv:comment: 30 pages, 8 figures and 6 tables, accepted for publication in JHEAP

entry.title: String Order in Quench Dynamics as a Probe of Quantum Phase Transitions
entry.summary: We study the anisotropic XY chain in a transverse field by introducing a global string order parameter and examining its equilibrium behavior and its quench dynamics from a fully polarized initial state. The corresponding string operator is defined as the product of local projected spin operators over the entire chain. The nonequilibrium order parameter is the long-time average of the logarithm of the string-operator expectation value per site after the quench. For the ground state, its field derivative is singular on the Ising critical lines; after the quench, the steady-state response also records the field boundaries and the anisotropy transition. We derive analytically the nonanalytic behavior of the order parameter at the quantum critical lines. Our results reveal a hidden nonlocal order underlying this paradigmatic model of conventional quantum phase transitions. They also connect measurable spin populations with equilibrium and dynamical topological structure.

entry.title: Radiation properties of a regular black hole embedded in a Dehnen-type dark matter halo with a thin accretion disk
entry.summary: We study the shadow, timelike geodesic structure, and thin accretion disk radiation properties of a static spherically symmetric regular black hole embedded in a Dehnen-type dark matter halo. Using the EHT observations of M87* and Sgr A*, we constrain the halo scale parameter $a$ at $1σ$ and $2σ$ levels. Based on the Page--Thorne model and a backward ray-tracing method, we compute the local radiative flux, redshift factor distribution, and observed flux images for different viewing angles. We further compare the Dehnen regular black hole with the Einasto and Hayward regular black holes by evaluating their ISCO radii and disk flux profiles. The results show that increasing $a$ reduces the ISCO radius, enlarges the effective radiation area, and amplifies the Doppler asymmetry of both direct and secondary images. Compared with the Einasto and Hayward models, the Dehnen black hole exhibits the strongest ISCO contraction and the most pronounced left-right brightness asymmetry, while the Einasto model is nearly insensitive to its scale parameter and the Hayward black hole shows only a mild dependence. These findings demonstrate that regular black holes with different regularisation mechanisms can be distinguished by their accretion disk images, providing a potential tool for testing dark-matter halo models with future high-resolution observations.

entry.title: CHEX-MATE: AMALGAM weak-lensing analysis of 41 Planck Sunyaev-Zel'dovich-selected galaxy clusters
entry.summary: We present a weak-lensing shear analysis of 41 Planck SZ-selected galaxy clusters at $0.11\le z\le 0.55$ from the CHEX-MATE sample, using wide-field Subaru/Suprime-Cam and CFHT/MegaPrime imaging from the AMALGAM project. We detect the azimuthally averaged weak-lensing signal around the X-ray peak of each cluster, achieving a median S/N of 6.5 per cluster. The $45^\circ$-rotated component has a median S/N of -0.1 and ranges from -1.8 to +1.8, consistent with zero. We model the excess surface mass density profile of each cluster with an NFW profile to infer weak-lensing mass and concentration constraints. The total systematic uncertainty in the weak-lensing mass calibration is assessed to be $8\%$. Using a hierarchical Bayesian framework, we then derive weak-lensing-calibrated scaling relations for the halo concentration, $c_{200}$, as a function of $M_{200}$ and redshift, and for the Planck SZ mass proxy, $M_{SZ}$, as a function of $M_{500}$ and redshift, while accounting for sample selection effects, weak-lensing modelling biases, and residual calibration uncertainty. At $M_{200}=10^{15}M_\odot$ and $z=0.25$, we find $c_{200}=3.53\pm0.71$ with an intrinsic scatter of $0.22\pm0.04$ dex. The inferred normalisation and scatter are consistent with recent $Λ$CDM predictions for massive haloes, with no significant mass or redshift dependence over the probed range. For the Planck mass proxy, our baseline regression yields $M_{SZ}/M_{500}=0.83\pm0.09$ at $M_{500}=7\times10^{14}M_\odot$ and $z=0.25$, with an intrinsic scatter of $0.10\pm0.02$ dex. A restricted model with fixed unit mass slope and no redshift evolution gives $1-b=0.72\pm0.11$. We also provide weak-lensing-calibrated posterior estimates of $M_{500}$ for the sample based on the baseline $M_{SZ}$--$M_{500}$--$z$ relation. These results provide an initial weak-lensing mass calibration for CHEX-MATE multi-probe cluster studies.

entry.title: Emulation of non-linear 1D spectral models: relativistic X-ray reflection
entry.summary: The use of machine learning techniques to approximate computationally expensive models has become increasingly prevalent in a wide variety of fields within astronomy. We discuss the implementation of emulators for 1-dimensional models in the context of the astrophysical numerical model reltrans, a black hole X-ray spectral model that models the effects of relativistically smeared emission from an accretion disk. We argue that the decision of whether and how to emulate should follow from a systematic characterisation of the target model, and we demonstrate a diagnostic workflow: examining how the spectrum varies with individual parameters. We adopt a modular strategy, emulating only the relativistically convolved reflection spectrum (1-10% of the total flux) rather than the full model. Using an operator-learning architecture with Fourier feature embeddings and FiLM conditioning, we reproduce the reflection spectrum to O(0.1)% precision across 0.1-100 keV with a 4-10x speed-up that scales considerably better under vectorised evaluation. This emulator, RTFAST2, recovers the true parameters of simulated observations without the systematic posterior biases of our previous work. We conclude that no architecture is universally transferable and bespoke emulators motivated by a model's specific structure are required. The modular approach taken in this work presents a promising strategy for future emulators of numerical models.

entry.title: First-Order Transitions in Weak Ising Spin-Orbit-Coupled Superconductors
entry.summary: Ising spin-orbit coupling (ISOC) can strongly protect superconductivity against exchange-field-induced depairing, typically leading to critical fields far exceeding the Pauli limit and continuous (second-order) phase transitions. Here, using a free-energy approach, we demonstrate that first-order transitions can emerge in superconductors with weak ISOC under large exchange fields. In this regime, conventional theoretical approaches based on the gap equation fail to determine the thermodynamic critical field and instead yield only the supercooling field. Moreover, we identify two pronounced in-gap coherence peaks in the quasiparticle spectra, which represent the weak-ISOC manifestation of the previously reported mirage-gap states. Our results establish the importance of free-energy analysis in describing the first-order phase transitions in Ising superconductors and reveal distinct spectroscopic signatures of the weak-ISOC regime.

entry.title: Decoupled asymmetric thin-shell wormholes
entry.summary: We construct reflection-asymmetric thin-shell wormholes by joining a Schwarzschild exterior to its minimal geometric deformation, which shares the same mass and redshift function, so that the asymmetry is carried entirely by the gravitational-decoupling sector. The deformed side is a black hole sourced by a scalar field coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics, in its branch with a real scalar. We show that the total radial null energy of shell and bulk obeys an exact identity and becomes positive for a sufficiently strong deformation. The momentum flux across the shell equals the radial null-energy density of the bulk, and retaining it yields the linear stability condition in closed form. We prove that stability with a conventional shell response requires the bulk to violate the radial null energy condition at the throat; the deformation instead enlarges the stable domain and moves the transition radius inside the photon sphere. For a stationary extension built on Kerr, the junction is solved exactly in the spin, which fixes how the angular momentum is shared between shell and bulk and where the shell behaves as a rotating fluid. A free-precession model provides an estimate of the gravitational-wave signal of the throat.

entry.title: Phase-Space Constraints on a General Class of Eckart-like Viscous Cosmologies
entry.summary: We study the cosmological dynamics of a general class of viscous dark matter models using a dynamical system analysis. In the Eckart formalism, these viscous cosmologies are characterized by a dimensionless bulk viscous pressure $Ω_Π\equiv Ω_Π(Ω_m)$, where $Ω_m$ is the matter density parameter. Our analysis demonstrates that a viable early radiation era requires the complete absence of viscosity, a proper matter-dominated epoch demands a small viscous pressure, and the only physically admissible late-time attractor is the cosmological constant-dominated fixed point; consequently, the background expansion must closely track standard $Λ$CDM evolution. We validate these general results using the power-law parameterization $Ω_Π= -\hatξ_0 Ω_m^s$, where $\hatξ_0$ and $s$ are real parameters; for $s \geq 1$ and $\hatξ_0 \ll 1$, the model reproduces the $Λ$CDM background, while for $s < 1$ the system encounters a past-time integration boundary where the dark matter density transitions into negative values and its viscous pressure evaluates to nonphysical complex numbers. Since the background expansion essentially duplicates $Λ$CDM, the model is unlikely to resolve the $H_0$ tension. However, large differences arise at the linear perturbative level; indeed, on sub-horizon scales, bulk viscosity causes a scale-dependent dissipative drag on the matter density fluctuations; this increases the Hubble friction, offering a channel to suppress structure growth.

entry.title: Calibration-Induced Systematics in SALT3 Training and Their Impact on Dark Energy Constraints from Stage IV Supernova Surveys
entry.summary: In the coming years, the Vera Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (Rubin-LSST) and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope's (Roman) High Latitude Time Domain Survey (HLTDS) are expected to discover more than a million Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia), several orders of magnitude more than current samples and with a tighter control on systematic uncertainties. One of the largest systematic uncertainties in cosmological analyses with SNe Ia is the accuracy of the spectrophotometric model for SNe Ia time series data, which depends on the photometric calibration of the surveys. To quantify the impact of this uncertainty, we analyze simulated Rubin-LSST and HLTDS data, perturb the photometric zero-points and filter mean wavelengths, and propagate these systematics to spectral model recovery, estimated distances, and dark energy Figure of merit (FoM) based on the $w_0 w_a$CDM model. Zero-point shifts of 5 mmag and filter mean wavelength shifts of 5 angstrom lead to a $\sim 50\%$ decrease in the FoM relative to a statistical-only case when calibration uncertainties are propagated only through light-curve fitting. The same calibration shifts applied only during model training produce a smaller $\sim 13\%$ degradation. Contrary to previous analyses, calibration uncertainties in light-curve fitting dominate over those from model training. Their effect during light-curve fitting varies smoothly with redshift and is nearly degenerate with cosmology, preventing mitigation through self-calibration. Finally, we show that the FoM dependence on the size of the calibration uncertainties (in the range of expected sizes) is roughly linear.

entry.title: Gravitational-Wave Signatures and Periodic Orbits of Charged Particles Around a Five-Dimensional Rotating Black Hole: Comparison with the Kerr Black Hole
entry.summary: We study periodic orbits of charged particles in the equatorial plane of a five-dimensional ($D=5$) rotating Myers--Perry black hole (BH) immersed in a uniform magnetic field, and the gravitational waves emitted by these orbits in an extreme mass-ratio inspiral. All results are compared with the Kerr BH in the uniform magnetic field. We find that a charged particle is much more weakly bound to the $D=5$ dimensional BH, i.e. its energy at the innermost stable circular orbit is close to unity, $0.95$--$0.99$, compared with $0.78$--$0.94$ for the Kerr BH, and the depth of the potential well is several times smaller. As a result, the periodic orbits of the $D=5$ dimensional BH lie much closer to the separatrix. The magnetic field can make the azimuthal frequency of the orbit smaller than the radial one and produces loops in the orbits far from the BH. Using the numerical kludge method, we compute the gravitational waveforms for a compact object of $10M_\odot$ orbiting a BH of $10^6M_\odot$. At the same magnetic field, the $D=5$ dimensional signal has a longer period, lower frequencies, and an amplitude smaller by about $18\%$. We show that for the magnetic parameter $βM=0.02$ the strongest spectral line is at $7.9$\,mHz, compared with $9.9$\,mHz for the Kerr BH. An estimate of the radiation reaction shows that the periodic orbits survive from less than an hour to a few days in the presence of an external magnetic field. Over these lifetimes, the signal-to-noise ratio for LISA is $7$--$31$ for the rotating BH in $D=5$ dimensions, compared to the Kerr BH where it is about $15$--$54$.

entry.title: Exact solutions for static spherically symmetric spacetime with a perfect fluid in Rastall theory
entry.summary: In general relativity, exact Liouvillian solutions for a static and spherically symmetric spacetime with a perfect fluid and the equation of state $p(r)=wρ(r)$ are known only for $w=0,-\frac{1}{6}, -\frac{1}{5}, -\frac{1}{3}$, and $-1$. We extend this setup to Rastall theory, presenting the relation between the Rastall parameter and the constant $w$, and deriving exact solutions that correspond to their known counterparts in general relativity, except for $w=-\frac{1}{6}$. Furthermore, we find that, when $w\neq \frac{1}{3}, -1$, there exist several types of solutions whose behaviors change depending on the choice of constants.
entry.arxiv:comment: 14 pages, Revised in response to referee comments

entry.title: How to Untwist Twisted Gauge Fields
entry.summary: This paper provides an isomorphism between the space of twisted gauge fields on a principal bundle $\mathcal{P}(M,H)$ and the space of standard gauge fields on a different principal bundle $\mathcal{Q}(M,G)$ associated to $\mathcal{P}$. This isomorphism extends to local fields on the base manifold, which enables the use of local twisted fields in standard gauge theories (e.g. Yang-Mills-like theories). This allows one to deal with two symmetry groups, coming from $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$, respectively. The construction makes use of a larger principal bundle $\mathcal{S}$ which has $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ as quotient bundles. $\mathcal{S}$ is a Hilsum-Skandalis bibundle between the action groupoids $H\ltimes\mathcal{P}$ and $G\ltimes\mathcal{Q}$. The gauge structure on $\mathcal{S}$ encodes both standard and twisted gauge structures on $\mathcal{P}$. In addition, the isomorphism classes of bundles $\mathcal{S}$ up to an isomorphism covering the identity map on $\mathcal{P}$ are in 1:1 correspondence with the equivalence classes of cocycles (up to a coboundary). This paper also provides a new interpretation of (full) dressing fields as dynamic (or active) sections of a principal bundle.

entry.title: Theory and Cosmology of Biverse Volume-Normalized Gravity
entry.summary: This dissertation expounds the biverse volume-normalized gravity, a novel theoretical framework of classical and quantum gravity that provides an unusual solution to the cosmological constant problem, the 60-degree-of-magnitude discrepancy between the value of the vacuum energy density in our universe predicted by particle physics and that implied by cosmological data. In the literature, there exist two interesting ideas: 1) to use the "volume-normalized" action functional, the usual action of the particle Standard Model and general relativity but divided by the spacetime volume, first proposed by Tseytlin; 2) to generate the vacuum energy density dynamically by assigning a ghost-free massive potential to the graviton. However, each has a problem: Tseytlin's attempt suffers from diverging quantum loops and the massive gravity theory has a second metric tensor with questionable origin and the quantum strong coupling problem. Inspired by these two ideas, as well as the AdS/CFT correspondence in string theory, the biverse volume-normalized gravity extends Tseytlin's idea by placing our (3+1)-dimensional universe on the boundary of a (4+1)-dimensional bulk space. This new adaptation controls the large quantum gravity loops in the limit of vanishing ratio of the spacetime volume of our universe to that of the other universe. The ghost-free massive gravity can then be seamlessly incorporated, not only that its otherwise nebulous second metric tensor appears naturally as the pullback of the bulk metric on the boundary, but its strong coupling problem also solved. The biverse volume-normalized gravity is also consistent with all tested models of particle cosmology and the evolution of the universe, and nontrivially predicts that the tensor-to-scalar ratio of our universe is exactly zero.

entry.title: Momentum-resolved thermodynamics and barrier-free order-parameter collapse in spin-orbit-coupled superconductors under a Zeeman field
entry.summary: Spin-orbit coupling (SOC) can enhance the critical Zeeman field of clean superconductors beyond the Pauli limit. We develop a momentum decomposition of the zero-temperature free energy to investigate spin-singlet $s$-wave superconductors with general time-reversal-symmetric SOC. The SOC component perpendicular to the Zeeman field enhances the critical field and suppresses first-order features, whereas the parallel component favors Pauli-limited thermodynamic behavior. Applying this framework to Rashba superconductors and Ising superconductors with weak Rashba SOC, we identify the origin of the abrupt collapse of the superconducting order parameter at the critical field. Competing angular contributions produce a nearly flat free-energy landscape, allowing a barrier-free order-parameter collapse distinct from the conventional Pauli-limited first-order transition.

entry.title: Revisiting supernova constraints on dark gauge bosons
entry.summary: We revisit the supernova constraints on three well-motivated light gauge bosons: the dark photon, the $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge boson, and the $U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ gauge boson. For the dark photon and the $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge boson, we re-evaluate the nucleon bremsstrahlung process within the one-pion exchange approximation, retaining the full momentum and mass dependence. The geometrical dependence of the decay and absorption of these gauge bosons inside the supernova core is also taken into account. Updated bounds on these models are derived based on the cooling of SN1987A and energy deposition constraints from low-energy supernovae (LESNe). Taking the SFHo-18.8 $18.8\,M_\odot$ profile, the SN1987A cooling constraints reach masses of about $230$ MeV, $280$ MeV, and $300$ MeV for the dark photon, the $U(1)_{B-L}$ boson, and the $U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ boson, while the corresponding LESN limits extend to about $450$ MeV, $440$ MeV, and $600$ MeV, respectively. The kinetic mixing parameter $ε$ for dark photon, the gauge coupling $g_{BL}$ in the $U(1)_{B-L}$ model, and the gauge coupling $g_{μτ}$ for the $U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ model are constrained down to $5.8\times10^{-12}$, $2.9\times10^{-16}$, and $6.4\times10^{-12}$, respectively.

entry.title: Multipartite dynamics beyond bipartite entanglement equilibration
entry.summary: Entanglement equilibration need not mark the end of quantum-information dynamics in quantum thermalization. We show that the complete Schmidt spectra of a fixed tripartition can become stationary while its multipartite correlation structure, distinguished by local-unitary invariants, continues to evolve. This separation occurs exactly within a finite window in self-dual kicked-Ising dynamics and asymptotically in Haar-random circuits. We further demonstrate an independently tunable timescale for multipartite dynamics using quantum-error-correcting codes. When coupled to a locally scrambling bath, ordinary entanglement approaches equilibrium through rapid local scrambling, while weak logical--bath coupling drives a slower reorganization of multipartite correlations. These results reveal a deeper distinction than the ordering of equilibration times: bipartite entanglement and multipartite correlation structure can probe distinct physical channels of quantum-information dynamics, rather than merely different stages of the same relaxation process.

entry.title: Time-domain framework for the Teukolsky equation with a particle source using comoving hyperboloidal coordinates
entry.summary: We present a scheme and implementation code for time-domain integration of the Teukolsky equation in 1+1 dimensions with a point-particle source, based on comoving, spatially compactified hyperboloidal coordinates. We demonstrate that the scheme evades the problem of nonphysical growing modes that plague some numerical evolution schemes without compactification. Our use of comoving coordinates greatly simplifies the application of jump conditions on the particle's worldline. We develop our method and test its performance for a scalar field on a Schwarzschild background, first for a circular geodesic orbit source and then for a scattering geodesic orbit. We then present a test implementation of the method for the $s = -2$ Teukolsky equation, illustrating its long-term stability and absence of growing-mode behavior through comparison with similar results using noncompactified characteristic coordinates. Our method paves the way to calculations of the full gravitational self-force in extreme-mass-ratio scattering.

entry.title: Ultra-compact twin stars with hybrid equations of state from bosonic dark matter
entry.summary: The properties of compact stars with a strong first-order phase transition to quark matter and with an additional fluid of self-interacting bosonic dark matter (DM) are studied. We find that the inclusion of DM changes the stability of mass-radius configurations relative to the naive one-fluid criterion. For compact star configurations with similar masses and different radii, so-called twin stars, the presence of DM removes the unstable segment between the hadronic and the hybrid branch, so that the stable mass-radius sequence becomes continuous after the onset of the phase transition to quark matter. We furthermore find stable ultra-compact objects (UCOs), defined by a total compactness $C = M_\text{tot}/R_\text{grav} \ge 1/3$. We observe two distinct classes of UCOs: a DM-halo class with $f_\text{DM} \gtrsim 0.9$, and a DM-core class at $f_\text{DM} \lesssim 0.02$. The two classes can be separated by the surface redshift of the normal matter, which reaches $z = 0.734 - 0.808$ for the DM-core and extreme values of $z = 2 - 3.468$ for the DM-halo class, allowing us to use their redshift as a way to disentangle the two classes. Furthermore, the high redshift of the DM-halo UCOs could serve as a signal of DM since their redshift exceeds the Buchdahl limit of $z = 2$. Finally, we find hybrid star solutions of ``ultimate twins" with similar masses and visible radii, but different dark matter content, leading to different tidal deformabilities and surface redshifts. Future X-ray and gravitational measurements of ultra-compact neutron stars with radii and masses outside the allowed neutron star range can thereby probe the presence and the properties of DM in addition to a first-order phase transition to quark matter.

entry.title: Direct observation of a spin-polarized surface Dirac gap in the antiferromagnetic topological insulator NdBi
entry.summary: A gapped Dirac cone in antiferromagnetic topological insulators (AFM-TIs) is essential for realizing the quantized anomalous Hall effect, yet its intrinsic magnitude remains controversial. In the prototypical AFM-TI MnBi2Te4, however, the observed Dirac gap is significantly smaller than theoretical predictions or nearly absent, highlighting a long-standing discrepancy. Here we demonstrate that NdBi hosts a spin-polarized topological surface Dirac cone with a sizable gap of 17 meV at the Dirac point, in excellent agreement with density functional theory predictions (12 meV). This direct observation is enabled by high-resolution 7 eV laser-based spin- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, which unambiguously disentangles the spin-polarized surface Dirac cone from bulk-derived states. Furthermore, through temperature dependence and controlled surface contamination, we establish a direct linkage between surface magnetism and the Dirac gap, demonstrating that the gap opens only in the presence of surface magnetic order. These results provide definitive spectroscopic evidence for an intrinsic Dirac gap in AFM-TIs and establish NdBi as a model platform to resolve the long-standing discrepancy between experiment and theory in AFM-TIs.

entry.title: Anisotropic magneto-elastic coupling in the quasi-2D Ising magnet Li$_2$FeSiO$_4$ and thermodynamic signature of low-energy orbital excitations
entry.summary: The relevance of spin, lattice and orbital degrees of freedom in the quasi-2D Ising-like magnet Li$_2$FeSiO$_4$ is demonstrated by thermal expansion and specific heat measurements supported by numerical studies. By means of thermodynamic and Grüneisen analysis, we separate the orbital signatures and quantify the energy gap and its pressure dependence from the experimental data as $Δ\sim 300 - 350$ K and $\partial \ln Δ/\partial p_{\rm c} \approx -4.6$ %/GPa). Both values excellently agree with the theoretical DFT predictions. The thermal expansion anomalies associated with the onset of long-range magnetic order imply significant magneto-elastic coupling and are used to determine the anisotropic uniaxial strain dependencies of $T_{\rm N}$. They are dominated by the in-plane (i.e., $c$ axis) response $(\partial \ln{ T_{\rm N}} )/\partial p_{\rm c} \simeq 15$ %/GPa while the (negative) $a$ axis and (positive) out-of-plane ($b$ axis) pressure dependencies are much smaller. Short-range magnetic order extends well above $T_{\rm N}$ but is not driven by the same energy scale as $T_{\rm N}$ as evidenced by the observation of non-monotonic in-plane distortion, sign-change of the Grüneisen parameter, and failure of Grüneisen scaling.

entry.title: Perturbative anomalies in quantum mechanics
entry.summary: In this work, we propose a cohomological approach to studying perturbative anomalies in quantum mechanics. The Hamiltonian $\hat{H}$ together with the symmetry generator $\hat{S}$ forms a unitary representation of the two-dimensional Abelian Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}\cong \mathbb{R}^{2}$ on the Hilbert space $V$. We show that perturbations of such a system are related to the first Chevalley-Eilenberg cohomology group $H^{1}_{CE}(\mathbb{R}^{2},\mathfrak{u}(V))$. In turn, the perturbative anomalies of the symmetry $\hat{S}$ are related to the second cohomology group $H^{2}_{CE}(\mathbb{R}^{2},\mathfrak{u}(V))$.

entry.title: A Simple Necessary and Sufficient Condition for Yang--Baxter Integrability
entry.summary: Quantum integrability is a cornerstone of the exact theory of interacting quantum spin chains. In its standard formulation, however, one starts from R-matrices satisfying the Yang--Baxter equation, rather than from the Hamiltonian itself. It has therefore remained unclear how Yang--Baxter solvability can be characterized directly at the Hamiltonian level, and how it is related to the existence of local conservation laws. Here we prove that, in a broad standard setting, the Reshetikhin condition is not only necessary but also sufficient for Yang--Baxter integrability, thereby reducing the hidden algebraic structure of integrability to a Hamiltonian-level conservation law. Since the Reshetikhin condition is equivalent to conservation of the total energy current, this Hamiltonian-level criterion is also experimentally accessible. This result establishes a quantum counterpart of the Liouville--Arnold theorem for isotropic spin chains, stating that Yang--Baxter solvability is equivalent to an infinite hierarchy of local conserved quantities. Our result also simplifies substantially the search for integrable spin chains by replacing the search for R-matrices with a direct criterion on local Hamiltonians.

entry.title: Surface-induced vortex core restructuring in a spin-triplet superfluid
entry.summary: Observing the structure of quantized vortices can provide evidence for the pairing nature of a superfluid or superconductor and pinpoint its order parameter. Spin-triplet superfluid $^3$He supports a variety of vortices, calculated and identified so far in bulk fluid. We show numerically that the vortex core in $^3$He is strongly altered near a surface, resulting in a structure inhomogeneous along the vortex line. The effect is asymmetric with respect to the relative orientation of the core order parameter anisotropy axis and the surface normal. Coupling of spin and orbital degrees of freedom in the gradient energy of a triplet order parameter allows the surface to lift the degeneracy of two bulk vortex states connected by spontaneously broken inversion symmetry of the core. In a wide range of external conditions, the vortex structure at the surface is found to be completely different from that in bulk. As an implication, surface-limited vortex core observations in a triplet-candidate system may not reflect the bulk structure. We propose an experimental verification of the effect by measuring a transition in the vortex structure in thin slabs of superfluid $^3$He-B.
